newsitem.title: FRANCE: De Silguy-no need for undue haste in EMU fx rates.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy-no need for undue haste in EMU fx rates.

text.p: European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Monday he saw no need for undue haste in deciding the method for fixing currency rates among countries joining monetary union.
He had been asked whether he thought this could be decided this year.

"The Commission has not made any proposals, it will do so at the appropriate time...We have to look at a certain number of questions, but I would say there should be no undue haste," he told Reuters during a ministerial meeting of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development.

Luxembourg Foreign Minister Jacques Poos said earlier this month that Luxembourg would push for an early decision on setting indicative exchange rates for countries joining Economic and Monetary Union to prevent market speculation.
Luxembourg takes over the European Union's rotating presidency in July.

Under the Maastricht treaty, exchange rates of countries joining monetary union cannot technically be fixed until the launch of the euro on January 1, 1999. But ministers are considering giving indicative rates early, by making an announcement ahead of time on how they plan to fix the rates.
